title: Streaming-first structured-response PRD: tool handshake, backoff & repair acceptance
creator: Aisha Raman
description: PRD defines acceptance criteria and testable requirements for a streaming-first structured output contract that supports function/tool handshake, robust backoff, checkpointed partial emits, and automated repair/reconciliation flows. This scope targets hosted and dedicated modes and aims to reduce production failures from partial or malformed emits during tool handoffs.
background: Multiple customers and internal observability have shown recurring failures when models emit structured frames interleaved with tool invocation signals. Failures cluster around network interruptions, tool gateway 5xxs, and schema drift during long-running streams. Current behavior lacks consistent repair semantics and operator-visible checkpoints for resuming without user-visible duplication or loss.
goals: Define deterministic handshake semantics between model-stream frames and tool-invocation envelopes
Specify backoff and retry policies that preserve idempotency and avoid duplicate side effects
Provide checkpointed partial-emits so consumers can resume from last validated frame
Surface clear telemetry and alerting thresholds for schema deviation and tool-call failures
Enable canary/A-B rollout gating with automatic fallback to non-streaming or last-known-good model when thresholds exceed limits
non_goals: Implementing new tooling runtime (this PRD focuses on contract and acceptance criteria only)
Full UI for replay/repair (ops will use raw logs and dashboards initially)
Guaranteeing third-party tool-side idempotency beyond our token/marker conventions
acceptance_criteria: Schema handshake: First stream frame must include a single-line 'schema_v' header with a semver string; runtime rejects streams missing header with a 400 and a clear error code 'ERR_SCHEMA_MISSING'

Progress frames: Model may emit zero or more 'progress' frames (type: 'partial_object') which must be checkpointed by the gateway with increasing sequence numbers; checkpoints persisted for at least 24 hours
Tool invocation envelope: Tool-call frames include 'call_id' (uuid), 'idempotency_token' (sha256 hex) and 'expected_ack_timeout_ms' fields; gateway must translate to upstream tool call headers

Backoff and retry: For tool gateway 5xx or network failures, gateway retries with exponential backoff (initial 150ms, multiplier 2, max attempts 4). Retries must include same idempotency_token; on repeated failure the stream emits a 'call_failed' frame with 'reason' and 'retryable' boolean

Soft-fallback: Consumer-facing stream must not block indefinitely; if all retry attempts fail, the runtime emits a 'fallback' frame advising fallback model or mode and transitions to best-effort logging mode

Resume and repair: Consumer can request resume from last persisted checkpoint sequence; when resume occurs the gateway must provide 'resume_proof' metadata and a reconciliation window of up to 5s to reconcile side-effecting tool calls

Duplicate suppression: If a tool call completes but the model/consumer receives no ack and retries, runtime tool proxy must detect duplicate idempotency_token and reply with a 200+duplicate flag rather than re-executing side effects

Observability: Each stream must produce events for handshake, each tool-call start/finish, retry attempts, and checkpoint persistence. Dashboards must show 95th percentile handshake latency < 120ms and per-route tool retry rate < 0.5% in steady-state
E2E tests: Automated CI tests simulate network partitions and tool 5xxs; acceptance requires stream resume and reconciliation to pass in 9/10 runs without duplicated side effects
Canary gating: New streaming schema or handler rollout must be gated by canary where errors do not exceed 0.2% or must auto-fallback to stable behavior
test_plan: Unit tests for header validation and schema_v parsing
Integration tests for checkpoint persistence and resume_proof correctness (mock store)
Chaos tests: introduce TCP drops and tool 500s; assert resume + reconciliation semantics and duplicate suppression
Load test with sustained 1k concurrent streams to validate checkpoint latency and telemetry aggregation
Manual exploratory: operator follows reproduction steps and validates dashboard alerts and logs
implementation_notes: Handshake header should be single-line for streaming parsers and kept small to avoid buffer thrashing
Persist only sequence -> checksum -> timestamp for checkpoints to limit storage costs; full object snapshots optional for critical routes
Use existing idempotency-token service for token generation/validation to leverage current dedupe tabels
Expose a 'stream_inspector' trace hook in the console to visualize partial emits and call envelopes during canary
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased latency from checkpoint persistence. Mitigation: use async durable queue and hedged persistence with local memcache to short-circuit resume
Risk: Upstream tools not honoring idempotency headers. Mitigation: mark such integrations as 'best-effort' and require operational runbook; track per-integration duplicate rate
Risk: Schema skew across model versions. Mitigation: support schema_v negotiation matrix and reject unsupported older schema versions during handshake
operator_playbook: When 'ERR_SCHEMA_MISSING' > 0.1%: Start roll forward to rollback map, notify model-onboarding team and pause new model rollouts
When per-route retry rate > 1% for > 5m: Switch route to fallback model variant and open incident
For duplicate-side-effects > threshold: Freeze outbound tool invocations for that integration and run dedupe migration script
design_feedback: Design: prefer a compact schema header to keep streaming parsers simple (approved)
Eng: request for asynchronous checkpointing to avoid p99 latency regressions (accepted with hedged write pattern)
PM: add explicit 'resume_proof' requirement to ensure operator confidence during audits (added)
